title: Brandon McNulty Wins Cycling World Title in Montreal — First American Since 1993
summary: Imagine riding a bike for more than six hours straight. That's what Brandon McNulty did on Sunday in Montreal — and he won! McNulty, 28, became the first American since 1993 to win the elite road race world title at the UCI Road World Championships. He made his big move with 33 kilometres to go and never let anyone catch him. His final time was 6 hours, 17 minutes and 4 seconds. "Until the last 300 metres, I really didn't even believe it," McNulty said. "I was just dying, but I just kept pushing." The race was 273.4 kilometres long — that's like riding from Montreal to Toronto and back! It went around a 13.4-kilometre circuit 12 times, with crowds of fans cheering. McNulty wasn't even one of the favourites to win. Two-time champion Tadej Pogacar was out with an injury, which made the race wild and unpredictable. Michael Matthews of Australia came second, and Matthew van der Poel of the Netherlands came third. The top Canadian was Michael Leonard of Oakville, Ont., who finished 32nd. McNulty said his team rode "crazy well" and called his win "a miracle."
why_it_matters: McNulty rode for more than six hours and kept pushing even when he felt he was 'dying' — it shows that big, hard goals are reached by training and not giving up.

background_read: The UCI (the group that runs international cycling races) gives the road race world champion a special jersey with rainbow stripes to wear for the whole next year.
Montreal is a big city in Canada, in the province of Quebec, and huge crowds stood along the streets to cheer the riders.
The last American to win this race did it in 1993 — more than 30 years before McNulty.
Article_Structure: WHO: Brandon McNulty, a 28-year-old American cyclist, plus rivals Michael Matthews of Australia, Matthew van der Poel of the Netherlands and Canadian rider Michael Leonard
WHAT: McNulty won the elite road race world title at the UCI Road World Championships, finishing in 6 hours, 17 minutes and 4 seconds
WHERE: Montreal, Canada — 12 laps of a 13.4-kilometre circuit, in a race 273.4 kilometres long
WHY: He attacked with 33 kilometres to go and held on, becoming the first American winner since 1993

perspectives.description: They say the win felt like 'a miracle' and that the whole team rode 'crazy well', so it was a group effort as much as one rider's speed.
Some might say the race was easier because two-time champion Tadej Pogacar was out with an injury, so the strongest riders never got to race.
The home crowd got a big day of racing, but the best Canadian, Michael Leonard, finished 32nd, so home fans went home without a podium place.
